messages:
Nora (customer): Hey team - since ~2026-03-09 our streaming calls to /v1/stream have had a big jump in first-byte latency (p95 ~600ms, p99 ~1.2s). Non-streaming completions to the same model look normal. No code changes on our side. Any ideas?

Alex (support): thanks Nora — can you paste a curl repro and the region you hit? Also last successful time you saw normal TTFB?

Nora (customer): repro below hitting us-east-1. Last normal was 2026-03-08.

curl --http2 -v "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","prompt":"hello","stream":true}'

Observing:
- TCP connect + TLS 20-30ms
- request sent fast
- first chunk delayed ~600ms then chunks stream normally

Alex (support): got it, reproducing now from my laptop hitting us-east-1. Will post timings.

Alex (support): repro steps I used:

# measure ttfb with curl
```
curl -w "time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer}\n" --http2 -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer x" -d '{"stream":true,"model":"redwood-7b","prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```

Observed time_starttransfer ~0.62s (consistent with your numbers). If I switch to non-streaming endpoint same model -> ~0.08s.

Priya (sre): tagging infra team — @Miguel any recent edge/proxy changes around 2026-03-09? We rolled an envoy upgrade around then.

Miguel (runtime): We did flip a low-level coalescing opt for the edge proxy last week to reduce small-packet overhead (was part of h2 write coalescer tuning). The intention was to lower backend CPU and reduce token churn. I was worried it might affect first-chunk timing in some cases.

Miguel (runtime): Hypothesis: the write coalescer is aggregating small writes from the runtime into a single flush, and the runtime used to emit an initial small chunk that forced a flush. With the coalescer enabled, that small initial write is being held until it reaches a threshold or timer -> delayed TTFB.

Alex (support): that matches what we see: total completion time unchanged but first chunk delayed. Non-streaming gets full payload so no delay.

Sara (cs): customer impact: p95 spikes are causing UX issues for chat. Nora, would you be able to test a short patch we can toggle on the edge?

Nora (customer): yes we can test. If there's a header toggle or alternate route that's easiest.

Miguel (runtime): Short-term mitigations:
- Option A: disable the coalescer for the streaming route (edge config). This should restore previous behaviour immediately.
- Option B: make runtime send a forced zero-length flush or an explicit 1-byte chunk as the very first write when stream=true (patch in runtime).
- Option C: fallback the customer to non-streaming for time-sensitive flows (not ideal).

Priya (sre): I'm going to push a canary disabling the coalescer for the streaming route in us-east-1 at 1% and watch ttfb metrics.

deploy-bot: canary config change requested by priya: disable-h2-coalesce for route /v1/stream -> initiating canary 1% (us-east-1)

infra-bot: canary started (id=cc-2026-03-12-01), monitoring metrics: stream.first_byte_p50/p95/p99

Priya (sre): @Alex @Miguel early numbers from the canary: p95 dropped from ~610ms -> ~95ms on canary hosts. p99 improved too. Looks promising.

Nora (customer): can confirm — after we were routed to a canary host our UI showed first-byte back to normal for a few sessions.

Alex (support): great. Deploy plan? Full rollback of coalescer or targeted opt-out for streaming?

Miguel (runtime): prefer targeted opt-out for streaming routes (less perf regression for other workloads). I'll open a runtime PR to force first-chunk flush when stream=true and also add an explicit header we can use at the edge (x-rw-force-flush: 1). That will be backward compatible.

Miguel (runtime): PR: send 1 byte + flush as the first write for streaming flows. Also add config knob to toggle behavior per route. Will link PR in a minute.

Alex (support): good plan. For customers who can't wait we can flip the edge opt-out per org temporarily. @Sara can you coordinate with Nora for org-level toggle?

Sara (cs): on it. Nora — want me to enable the org toggle for you so you can validate immediately?

Nora (customer): yes please, that would help. Thanks.

Sara (cs): done — enabled coalescer-disable for NoraCorp in us-east-1. Please retest.

Nora (customer): retest now — first-byte ~90ms. Looks fixed for our traffic pattern. Thank you! :tada:

Miguel (runtime): I'll push the runtime PR and aim for a small release tomorrow; prefer automation + tests to avoid regressions. Also will add a unit test to ensure first write flushes under stream=true.

Priya (sre): I'll keep canary running another 2h then sweep to 100% for streaming routes if metrics hold. We'll also add an alert for a sudden divergence between streaming.ttfb and nonstream.ttfb so we catch regressions faster.

Alex (support): I'll follow up with a short postmortem and timeline (include which change caused it, mitigations, and how to test).

Nora (customer): much appreciated. Your fast response here saved our demo this morning.

Miguel (runtime): FYI for the postmortem I'll include the PR ref, the edge config key, and a short explanation of coalescer behavior and thresholds.

deploy-bot: canary sweep to 100% scheduled by priya at 2026-03-12T15:20Z if no regressions.

Alex (support): closing loop — action items:
- Miguel: PR to force-first-flush + config (ETA 24h)
- Priya: canary -> 100% if green, set alert for stream vs nonstream TTFB disparity
- Sara: org toggle for Nora validated
- Alex: write incident note + customer summary

Nora (customer): thanks everyone, happy to validate further if needed.

Alex (support): thanks all. We'll update the PM/incident channel when we roll the runtime change.
